question.problem:
The inverse of the matrix $B$ is found using row operations, as shown below. What are the row operations corresponding to each step?

$$
\begin{aligned}[B\,|\,I] & =[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & -3 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}] &  & \text{___________} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 & -\frac{1}{3}\end{aligned}] &  & \text{___________} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 1 & -\frac{2}{3} \\ 0 & 1 & 0 & -\frac{1}{3}\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$
question.worked_solution:
We write down $B$ and the identity matrix $I$ side-by-side (as shown below) and apply the standard Gauss-Jordan method to transform the matrix $B$ into the identity matrix. We perform the same row operations on both matrices:

$$
\begin{aligned}[B\,|\,I] & =[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & -3 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :=-\frac{1}{3}{R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 & -\frac{1}{3}\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & :={R}_{1}+2{R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 1 & -\frac{2}{3} \\ 0 & 1 & 0 & -\frac{1}{3}\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

The corresponding row operations are

$$
{R}_{2}:=\frac{1}{3}{R}_{2},\,{R}_{1}:={R}_{1}+2{R}_{2}.
$$

The matrix ${B}^{-1}$ is given by the right-hand side of our big matrix after all of the transformations have been completed. Therefore, 

$$
{B}^{-1}=[\begin{aligned}1 & -\frac{2}{3} \\ 0 & -\frac{1}{3}\end{aligned}].
$$
